title: A Smart Privacy Commodity: a Quantitative Model of Dynamic Pricing Strategy

source.relative_path: 2018美赛特等奖/F题4篇/F88508-A Smart Privacy Commodity a Quantitative Model of Dynamic Pricing Strategy.pdf

context_sources.name: Acquisti, Taylor and Wagman, the economics of privacy
Mon, entropy-weighted fuzzy analytic hierarchy process
Slovic and Peters, risk perception and affect

limitations: Many equations are flattened, especially the consistency tradeoff, the transition matrix and the equilibrium quotes.
Table 1 rows are misaligned, so several symbols are ambiguous.
The value states are said to number six but the starting row has five entries.
The conclusion names the year 2012 twice instead of 2012 and 2032.
Policy and culture correction factors are named and never estimated.

tasks: Price privacy at the person, group and nation level
Weight four fields by hierarchy and entropy
Capture generational differences and network effects
Model policy and culture at the national level
Define the risk per field and assign responsibility
Test against real data and check stability

section_map.summary: Two sub-problems, three scales, a 783 dollar national price.
Two rights, three sensitivity grades, a claim after a leak.
Privacy as a tradable good, four fields, three levels.
Seven assumptions from supply control to identity theft.
Entropy plus hierarchy weights, TOPSIS, consistency tradeoff.
Multi-tree subgroups, five-factor risk, a Markov chain.
Bayesian Nash market, three policies, culture, externality.
Risks per field and group, expected loss, responsibility.
Gap within 0.17, three confessed errors, a swap test.
Strengths, data weakness, dynamic game as future work.

contributions.summary: A weight that joins judgment and data through one share.
A national price read off the crossing of two quote curves, at 783.
An externality correction added at every level.

dependency_graph.handoff: The consistency tradeoff enters the group's privacy-type term
Group risk perception is adjusted by the national sharing climate
The priced records are the ones whose risk is then measured

assumptions.summary: People control the supply of their data and it is a measurable good.
Government rules bind and move supply and demand.
A leak joins an identity-theft ring.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Real data from Acquisti, FERPA and EEOC, supplemented by McSherry and simulation.
Six personal traits and four fields, features from the most cited paper in each.
The same Acquisti data used again to test, gap within 0.17.

models.summary: Combined weights, TOPSIS score, consistency tradeoff.
Five-factor risk perception and a Markov chain of values.
Bayesian Nash quotes plus policy, culture and externality.
Expected loss split into human rights and property.

verification.summary: Willingness to share by age within 0.17 of the published data.
Swapping a few features moves the result little; swapping many moves it a lot.

results_trace.summary: Willingness to share peaks between 20 and 30 and falls with age.
Buyer and seller curves meet at 783 dollars.
Health records price above the other three fields.

writing_logic.summary: The problem is split into price and risk before any method.
Each weighting method is given its flaw before they are joined.
A contrast between risk and value justifies stripping identifiers.

language_observations.summary: One split produces a rule for each of three cases.
Two methods are each faulted, then reconciled by a formula.
A market fact is turned into a named class of game.
Three limitations are confessed in a fixed order.

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 2: traits and fields by level.
Figure 3: hierarchy, entropy and combined weights.
Figure 4: TOPSIS pricing in four fields.
Figure 5: consistency tradeoffs in four fields.
Figure 9: risk perception over fifty years.
Figure 10: prices by age and field.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The 783 dollar price is read off a figure with no tabulated quotes.
The 0.17 bound is stated without the per-age comparison shown.
Six value states are claimed but five numbers are given.

weaknesses.summary: Some models stay theoretical because the privacy-cost data could not be obtained.
Demographic sorting misses within-group differences and the forecast is short-run only.
Policy and culture corrections are named and never fitted.

independent_extensions.summary: Replace the static game with a dynamic, multi-party one.
Estimate the policy and culture correction factors.
Reconcile the six named value states with the five-entry row.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Give the person a claim against the controller after a leak.
Add the external value the trading parties do not capture.

unresolved_questions.question: What are the logistic and breach parameters?
What are the fitted policy and culture corrections?
